title: From Hearth to Snack Cake
premise: A playful journey through kitchens: make recognizable food, discover what living cultures and skilled processing change. Time is compressed; these are not complete cooking instructions.

recipes.description: Yeast changes the dough over time; the game compresses fermentation.
A suitable bacterial culture transforms milk; it is not the same culture as bread yeast.
Rubbing fat into flour makes a short pastry; water and handling are compressed here.
Cold butter is folded through dough in separate layers; this is not simply stirred together.
A filling is injected into a sponge cake. This is a broad snack-cake model, not a commercial formula.
A Twinkie-inspired endpoint: a wrapped golden sponge cake with a creamy filling. The brand formula and its industrial process are not reproduced.
A period menu organized through hot/cold and wet/dry qualities. This records a historical belief, not a medically effective diet.
A museum annotation distinguishes a historical explanatory system from present-day nutrition; neither is a literal ingredient.
Stir fruit into the yogurt. Neither ingredient is retired: both still have other uses.
Spread butter on the bread. This optional discovery is not a quota or a gate.

stages.title: The roadside hearth
stages.speaker: The traveller
stages.motivation: We have grain and fruit. Make flatbread and press a drink before the caravan leaves.

area.label: The roadside hearth
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

stages.completionText: Flatbread and fruit juice: enough for the road. The caravan can leave.

stages.title: The dairy and bakehouse
stages.speaker: The baker
stages.motivation: Our neighbours keep living cultures. Give us a risen loaf and a bowl of yogurt.

area.label: The dairy and bakehouse
area.travelText: We take our dough and fruit to the dairy and bakehouse. The pressed juice and flatbread remain at the roadside hearth.

caches.label: Dairy shelves
caches.narrative: The dairy keeps milk, cream, a churn and separate cultures for its bread and milk.

stages.completionText: A risen loaf and a bowl of yogurt. Two different cultures have changed what we brought.

stages.title: The pastry workshop
stages.speaker: The pastry cook
stages.motivation: Butter can crumble through flour or lie in thin sheets. Bring me a fruit tart and a puff pastry.

area.label: The pastry workshop
area.travelText: We bring the pastry ingredients and a loaf to the workshop. Cream and the churn come from the dairy; yogurt stays there unless we return for it.

caches.label: Pastry cupboard
caches.narrative: A working pastry kitchen holds eggs, sugar, whisks and old menu records as well as its ovens.

stages.completionText: A fruit tart and puff pastry: the butter made two very different textures.

stages.title: The small cake line
stages.speaker: The food historian
stages.motivation: Now a bakery wants its little sponge cake to travel. Make the filled, wrapped snack cake. Our last stop is a Twinkie-style cake, not a verdict that later food is better.

area.label: The small cake line
area.travelText: We are taking the useful things with us. Earlier creations remain where we made them.

caches.label: Cake-line stores
caches.narrative: The pilot line keeps filling ingredients and wrappers; the sponge-making tools came with us.

objectives.text: Make the wrapped Twinkie-style snack cake.

stages.completionText: The filled sponge cake is wrapped for its journey. From hearth to cake line, our short kitchen tour is complete.

notes: Prototype target: test whether tangible food transformations remain engaging across a shift to industrial production.
The branded final output is a fictional approximation. Hostess official page was unavailable to web reader; exact formula not asserted.
Humoral menu is an optional historical side discovery, never a nutrition recommendation. No medical efficacy mechanic.
Not a universal food chronology: fermentation and pastry have multiple regional histories. A Paris-style workshop does not claim France invented layered pastry.
Version2: item descriptions provide inspectable semantic content. Same recipe graph and checkpoints as v1; new text does not constitute human fun validation.

v3 adds two optional familiar discoveries requested by a fresh player: fruit yogurt and bread with butter. Explicit scene carry brings their ingredients without carrying every future-use thing. No new objective quota.
Presentation v5: stage completion acknowledgments and readable pre-use contents. Recipe graph unchanged from v3; no added quotas, themes or mechanics.
